He was baptized as a {{ill|Kirishitan|en|Kirishitan|qid=Q718714|lt=Kirishitan}} under the name '''Manoel (Manoel Aqui Marza)'''.

== Unresolved Matters ==
Akimasa's historical records are limited, leaving many details about his life unclear.

=== Adoption and Name Issues ===
Akimasa was the son of {{ill|Kadenokōji Aritomi|ja|勘解由小路在富|qid=Q11400104}} of the {{ill|Kamo clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏}} {{ill|Kaga no Kōji family|ja|勘解由小路家 (賀茂氏)}}, but it remains uncertain whether he officially succeeded the family headship.

=== Kirishitan Onmyōji ===
Akimasa is notable for being a Kirishitan onmyōji. Historical sources such as {{ill|Luís Fróis|en|Luís Fróis|qid=Q553687|lt=Luis Frois}}' {{ill|History of Japan|ja|日本史|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 日本の歴史|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q130436}} refer to "Aquimasadono," a high-Ranking astrologer and court noble, thought to correspond to Kamo no Akimasa.

== Biography ==

=== Early Life ===
Akimasa was born into the Kamo clan, a lineage traditionally tasked with the responsibilities of the {{ill|Onmyōryō|ja|陰陽寮}}, particularly in calendar and astronomical practices.

=== Conversion to Christianity ===
In {{ill|1560|en|1560|qid=Q6613|lt=1560}}, Akimasa encountered Jesuit missionaries, leading to his baptism as Manoel. He later relocated to {{ill|Bungo Province|en|Bungo Province|qid=Q864148|lt=Bungo Province}} with his family, where he became involved with the Christian community.

=== Return to Kyoto ===
After years in Kyushu, Akimasa returned to Kyoto, where he resumed his court duties. He received several court promotions, ultimately attaining the Rank of {{ill|Junior Fourth Rank|ja|従四位下|lt=Junior Fourth Rank, Lower Grade}}.

=== Later Years and Death ===
Akimasa died in {{ill|1599|en|1599|qid=Q6803|lt=1599}} at the age of 80 or 81. His son {{ill|Kaga no Kōji Akinobu|ja|勘解由小路在信}} is thought to have succeeded him briefly before the family's eventual decline.

== Cultural Appearances ==
* '''Video Games:''' Featured in "Oni Musha Soul" and "Sengoku Asuka ZERO."
* '''Literature:''' Depicted in historical novels like *Cross of the Onmyōji*.
